messages:
sec-alert-bot: ALERT: auth anomalies for user alice@customer.com — 18 concurrent sessions across 12 distinct IPs within 3m, token refresh rate 4x baseline. Possible credential stuffing or session token leak.
maya: noticed a surge in auth errors around 10:12 UTC. lots of token_refresh events in audit logs.
kevin: confirming — querying auth logs now. `select * from auth_events where user='alice@customer.com' and ts > now()-interval '1 hour'` returns repeated token_refresh + session_create from eu-west and us-east ranges.
priya: any impossible-travel signals? geos span 3 countries but timestamps overlap, so more likely session replay or parallel device abuse.
lena: also seeing increased rate of failed OTP pushes for other users in same tenant — MFA fatigue pattern maybe being abused.
sre-oncall: taking containment. will revoke all sessions for alice@customer.com and enable tenant-wide step-up for 1h.
kevin: run `authctl revoke-sessions --user alice@customer.com --reason "suspicious concurrency spike"` and paste output.
sre-oncall: `> revoked 18 sessions (ok)`. applied tenant step-up: require MFA for new sessions for 60m. :white_check_mark:
maya: checking KMS logs for suspicious key usage tied to service accounts — nothing abnormal in last 24h. KMS: `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/auth/cryptoKeys/jwt-sign` shows only expected signing calls by auth-service.
priya: good to know. is there any sign of compromised service account?
kevin: service-account creds look rotated last month, no unusual IAM policy changes in audit logs.
lena: I pulled a stacked timeline: session_create, token_refresh, ip_rotation every 10-20s — looks like automated client replay. likely credential stuffing or leaked refresh tokens.
maya: containment checklist: 1) revoked sessions (done), 2) tenant step-up (done), 3) blocked suspicious IPs from known cloud providers for this tenant (partial) — TBD, 4) create detection rule for high-concurrency per-user (TBD).
priya: for immediate mitigation, can we add a soft throttle on token refresh for this tenant? maybe 1 refresh per minute per user.
kevin: yes, we can push a rate-limit in the auth edge. I'll open a canary config: `auth-edge: token_refresh_rate_limit=1/m` for tenant acme-corp.
sre-oncall: implemented canary rate-limit for acme-corp in eu-west, monitoring.
maya: auditing: need an export of raw auth events for the 3h window around the spike for the incident ticket. Priya, can you take ownership?
priya: will export to s3://sec-incidents/1765432199/ and attach to ticket. will also redact PII.
lena: quick vuln-triage note: check if any legacy long-lived API tokens are provisioned for this tenant that bypass refresh controls. I found one service token last used 2 days ago — flagged.
kevin: add action: rotate that service token and rotate any KMS-wrapped service account keys in 24h.
maya: comms: recommend informing the tenant (ACME) privately: summarize actions taken and note that we blocked sessions and asked them to rotate creds. I'll draft an email.
priya: creating incident record in PagerDuty/Confluence with severity S2. link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/sec/incidents/1765432199 (placeholder).
kevin: post-incident tasks: 1) add detection rule: concurrent_sessions>5 within 5m OR refresh_rate>3x baseline, 2) reduce default token lifetime for web sessions from 30d -> 7d, 3) enforce re-auth for RPC clients after 24h, 4) update runbook for MFA-fatigue indicators.
sre-oncall: logging notes: audit logs currently sample non-interactive token events at 10% to reduce cost. increase sampling to 100% for token_refresh and session_create events for 48h for this tenant. I'll raise retention to 90d for these event types.
maya: also schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow with sec/responders + platform to review telemetry and rolling mitigations.
priya: file created: INC-1765432199, will link timeline and exports.
lena: assigned follow-ups: rotate svc token (kevin), detection rule (maya), write runbook update (priya), tenant comms (maya).
kevin: one more thing — check RBAC for support-bot accounts that can create sessions on behalf of users. ensure those tokens are time-bound.
maya: agreed. adding RBAC review to postmortem.
sre-oncall: monitoring shows decline in concurrent sessions after revocation and rate-limit. will leave enhanced monitoring for 24h.
priya: exporting logs now. ETA 12m.
maya: thanks all. set reminder for postmortem + apply the immediate config changes after review. :thumbsup:
sec-alert-bot: STATUS CHANGE: incident INC-1765432199 -> acknowledged.
